Crossed mixed PERMANOVA for incomplete, unequally replicated designs

Source: R/crossed-incomplete.R
permanova_crossed_incomplete.Rd

Fixed and random factors fully crossed, where cells may be empty and replication may be unequal. Sums of squares are marginal: each term is tested for what it adds to the model containing every other term. Denominators come from the design's expected mean squares, so a fixed term crossed with a random factor is tested over the stratum carrying the same random components, and falls back to a Satterthwaite combination when imbalance leaves no single stratum matching.

Usage

permanova_crossed_incomplete(
  design,
  hypothesis = c("II", "I", "III"),
  permutations = 999L,
  seed = NULL,
  keep_permutations = FALSE,
  max_exact = 100000L,
  tol = 1e-10
)

Arguments

design

A permanova_design from compile_permanova_design() with no /-generated nesting. Random terms are optional: with none, every term is tested over the residual, which is how an incomplete fixed design is handled.

hypothesis

Sums of squares. "II" (default) adjusts each term for every term that does not contain it. "I" is sequential, in the model matrix's term order. "III" adjusts each term for every other term in the model; on an incomplete design a term containing this one can span it, so Type III may report fewer estimable degrees of freedom than Type II – and in a saturated random model can drive a main effect to zero. Type II is the default because it stays well posed however incomplete the design is.

permutations

Number of Freedman-Lane permutations, or "all".

seed

Optional random seed.

keep_permutations

Retain the permutation statistics.

max_exact

Largest permutation space to enumerate exactly.

tol

Numerical tolerance for ranks.

Value

An object of class permanova_crossed_incomplete.

Details

Degrees of freedom are estimable dimensions, not level-count products. A term whose cells are partly empty reports the rank it actually spans, and nominal_df in the returned table records what a complete design would have given, so the loss is visible rather than silent.

Expected mean squares follow the restricted parameterisation – fixed effects summing to zero over mixed terms – so a random stratum carries no component from a random-by-fixed interaction sitting inside it.

See also

permanova_crossed() for complete, equally replicated designs.
